thread:
jules_ruby: registering a weird repro from the onboarding sampleapp: when STS token rotation happens mid-paginated scan, the client either stalls or fires a big burst depending on SDK. seen on Ruby and Py.
noah_py: ok can you sketch the flow? is this about prefetch/pagination?
jules_ruby: yes. sample pager prefetch=3. generate() does an auth handshake if access token expired. in Ruby auth is synchronous so the pager keeps pulling pages while the handshake blocks on net I/O -> we end up with a stalled worker and eventually connection_pool exhaustion.
jules_ruby: simplified snippet:
```ruby
pager.each do |page|
  client.generate(page.items) # may call TokenManager.refresh! which does an HTTP request
end
```
lee_devx: hmm interesting. py behaves differently?
noah_py: Python SDK uses an async refresh path (awaitable) in the default flow so the event loop yields and the pager naturally waits. but in sync mode py also can reproduce.
mira_pm: does the backend return 429s or do we just hit client-side socket limits?
jules_ruby: both, depending on timing. two failure modes observed:
- stall: threads blocked on auth, no work progresses, onboarding hangs.
- burst: refresh finishes and backlog of prefetched pages flood generate() causing transient 429s.
lee_devx: do you have logs?
jules_ruby: pasted short log:
```
[03:12:01] pager: enqueued page 4 (prefetch=3)
[03:12:01] tokenmgr: refresh start (url=https://sts.example.com)
[03:12:02] tokenmgr: refresh retry 1 (conn reset)
[03:12:02] pager: enqueued page 5
[03:12:02] pool: connections=0/10, waiting=6
[03:12:03] tokenmgr: refresh finish
[03:12:03] client: drain backlog=7 -> concurrent=8 (limit=4)
[03:12:03] backend: 429 too_many_requests burst
```
mira_pm: sounds like an SDK parity + prefetch hazard. product question: should onboarding sampleapp set prefetch lower by default?
lee_devx: propose short-term mitigation: reduce prefetched pages to 1 in sampleapp and add a note in onboarding guide about auth refresh hazards. medium-term: implement a token refresh strategy that yields control instead of blocking the pager thread.
noah_py: for Python we can keep async refresh; for Ruby we could make refresh spawn a helper thread and return a placeholder future or explicitly yield to the scheduler. that avoids blocking the pager's enumerator.
jules_ruby: i tried a hack: TokenManager.refresh_async { |t| token = t } which offloads refresh to a background thread and the pager pauses until token arrives -> stalls are gone but latency tail increases.
lee_devx: tradeoffs documented please. also add an integration test that simulates flaky STS (connection resets) and measures both queue_depth and connection waiters.
mira_pm: action items: 1) change sampleapp prefetch default to 1 and publish note (jules), 2) add Ruby change to offload refresh as opt-in (noah/jules), 3) add flaky STS integration test in CI (lee), 4) docs blurb about auth-backpressure and onboarding knobs (mira).
